newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS GO FIVE POINTS CLEAR AFTER OLD FIRM VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS GO FIVE POINTS CLEAR AFTER OLD FIRM VICTORY.

text.p: Rangers took another step towards equalling Celtic's record of nine successive Scottish league titles when they won the Old Firm derby 2-0 at Ibrox on Saturday.

Goals from Richard Gough after 51 minutes and Paul Gascoigne in the dying seconds gave Rangers victory against their arch-rivals who had defender Tosh McKinlay sent off for two bookable offences after 43 minutes.
It was the seventh time Celtic have had a player sent off this season and it was their fifth dismissal in the last five matches.

It was also Celtic's first league defeat in 38 matches and came almost a year to the day since their last loss -- also 2-0 against Rangers whose victory on Saturday gave them a psychological boost as they aim for their ninth successive title, a feat Celtic achieved from 1996 to 1974.
Saturday's victory moved Rangers, who have won all seven league matches five points clear of Celtic at the top of the Scottish premier division.
Celtic's miserable day started with a pre-match row between their manager Tommy Burns and Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooijdonk which saw the Dutchman left out of the team.
Celtic were also without injured Portuguese striker Jorge Cadette and lost German forward Andreas Thom with an injury early in the first half and that was too much for them to handle.
The Scottish title is again looking increasing like a two, or even one-horse race, with third placed Aberdeen already 10 points behind Rangers after losing 1-0 at Dundee United.

While Rangers won the Glasgow derby, Hearts triumphed in Edinburgh version, winning 3-1 at Hibernian with Colin Cameron scoring after 19 and 30 minutes and John Robertson adding a third five minutes before halftime, his 250th goal for the club. Darren Jackson pulled one back for Hibs with a 57th minute penalty.
Motherwell beat Kilmarnock 1-0 in a match marred by the 86th minute sending off of Motherwell's Jimmy Dolan and Kilmarnock's Derek Anderson for fighting.
